_comment: DIGITAL ASSET LINKS. This file is what makes the Android APK open
full-screen instead of inside a browser frame with an address bar.
A Trusted Web Activity only drops its browser chrome when Android can
prove the APK and this domain belong to the same owner. It proves that
by fetching https://nicotiamarket.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json and
matching the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the APK was signed
with against the list below. No match, no proof, and the app renders
as a Custom Tab, which looks broken, and is the single most common
reason a home-made TWA 'doesn't work'.
TO FILL THIS IN:
1. Build the APK (PWABuilder or Bubblewrap, see /android).
2. Both hand you a signing key and print its SHA-256 fingerprint.
PWABuilder puts it in signing.keystore + the generated
assetlinks.json in the zip; Bubblewrap prints it at the end and
can also emit one with `bubblewrap fingerprint generateAssetLinks`.
3. Replace REPLACE_WITH_SHA256_FINGERPRINT below with that value,
uppercase hex, colon-separated, e.g. AB:CD:12:...  (32 pairs).
4. Deploy, then check it is live and served as JSON:
curl -s https://nicotiamarket.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json
5. Verify Android accepts it:
https://developers.google.com/digital-asset-links/tools/generator
Keep the keystore safe and backed up. Android identifies an app by its
signing key: lose it and you cannot ship an update to anyone who
already installed, they have to uninstall and reinstall.
package_name must match the id you gave the generator. Leaving this
file live with the placeholder is harmless, Android simply finds no
match, exactly as it does today with no file at all.
This _comment key is ignored by Android; the parser reads the objects
and the fields it knows.
